# Graphical self-intros

## What's the purpose of a self-intro?
- To help others get to know you
- To help others understand your perspective
- To help others understand your values
- To help others understand your skills

## Your self-intros
- On Canvas > Files > `graphicalSelfIntros.pdf`
- Radically different sizes
- Some are stories, others are perhaps puzzles to solve
- No one included their name on the sketch
- Some revealed a lot of skill that you can perhaps share with others in the class

## Your good design sketches
- These are meant to help you reflect on what good design is
- They are also meant to refine your sketching skills
- Do not include screenshots or sketches by other people
  - If you want to include a design that was presented as a sketch, copy it using your own skills

# project ideas

## previous semester idea rejected, then reconsidered
- presented idea was to help women seeking abortions in Texas
- rejected because it seemed like more of a privacy and security issue than a UX issue
- reconsidered because I then researched it and found UX issues that weren't presented
- e.g., websites to help undocumented migrants assume literacy and often English literacy
- two synergistic groups: drivers and patients
- synergistic groups often overcome the so called *cold start* problem
- in other words, "this app will attract a lot of users once it's attracted a lot of users" (oops!)

- Collage
- Images
- Typography
- Color palettes

## Be like Karim
![](fiKarimRashid.png)

## Karim directives (excerpt)
<small>

::: {.container}
:::: {.col}
- Don't specialize
- Before giving birth to anything physical, ask yourself if you have created an original idea, an original concept, if there is any real value in what you disseminate.
- Know everything about the history of your profession and then forget it all when you design something new.
- Never say “I could have done that” because you didn’t.
- Consume experiences, not things.
::::
:::: {.col}
- Normal is not good.
- There are three types of beings—those who create culture, those who buy culture, and those who don’t give a shit about culture. Move between the first two.
- Think extensively, not intensively.
- Experience is the most important part of living, and the ex- change of ideas and human contact is all life really is. Space and objects can encourage increased experiences or distract from our experiences.
- Here and now is all we got
::::
:::

</small>

## Visit a design museum

##
![](fiPalacioDeBellasArtes.png)

::: {.notes}
I visited the Palacio de Bella Artes in Mexico City in 2012. It's not a design museum specifically, but it did give me a lot of design inspiration nonetheless.
:::

##
![](fiBorgesEnMexico.png)

::: {.notes}
At the time, they were featuring an exhibition on Edvard Münch, as well as this exhibition about a trip by Borges to Mexico.
:::

##
![](fiMuralByDiegoRivera.png)

::: {.notes}
The museum features a lot of work by Diego Rivera, including this admittedly overexposed mural. This overexposed mural is a good example of why you need to keep documenting things and learning as you go. I used to overexpose a lot more often than I do now. Also, I've stuck with basically the same camera, just different iterations of it.
:::

##
![](fiDiegoRiveraMural.png)

::: {.notes}
This mural by Diego Rivera was in the same room as the previous one.
:::

##
![](fiMuralInMexicoCity.png)

::: {.notes}
And this mural was in the street, at a construction site.
:::

##
![](fiFridaDiego.png)

::: {.notes}
On the same trip, I visited some of the homes of Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera which have been converted into museums. I think this is the only one where I got pictures.
:::

##
![](fiFridaDiegoHouse.png)

::: {.notes}
This is the view you see when you first enter the gate.
:::

##
![](fiFridasDesk.png)

::: {.notes}
This is Frida Kahlo's desk. I love to see the working environments of artists and I took a number of photographs of her workspace, a few of which follow. Workspaces in general are fascinating because we spend so much time in them.
:::

##
![](fiFridaDeskCloseup.png)

::: {.notes}
A closeup of one of her sketchbooks ...
:::

##
![](fiFridaPastelsInks.png)

::: {.notes}
Here are the pastels and inks on the right side of her desk.
:::

##
![](fiFridaPigmentsBrushes.png)

::: {.notes}
Here are some pigments and brushes sitting on the left.
:::

##
![](fiFridasKitchen.png)

::: {.notes}
Here is part of Frida's kitchen. Notice how she's made it an exciting place to be. The eye of the artist isn't just on the canvas, but on every aspect of life. Contrast this with the home of Einstein which is now a museum and reminds us that he was mostly living in his head.
:::

##
![](fiFridasPalette.png)

::: {.notes}
This is part of a larger exhibit, where this shows her color palette for the project. The notes on the left discuss the colors she used.
:::

##
![](fiKidzania.png)

::: {.notes}
This is a view of Kidzania, a working city for children with branches in Mexico City, Dallas, and, I think, a few other places. Here the children are getting dressed in preparation to work as painters.
:::

- Try @Dodson2006

# Crazy eights
![](fiCrazyEights.png)

## How to do it
- Choose a site or app to work on
- Make a list of screens needed
- Fold a large sheet into 8 squares
- Quickly draw a screen on each square (one minute per screen)
- Can be one screen eight times or eight diff screens or a combo

## Develop your own shorthand
For example

- a boxed $\times$ means a photo
- a circle means an icon
- a straight line means a headline
- a squiggly line means body copy
